solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Covered in blotches and wet earth in odd soggy parts

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as something sits in a box
the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth, are the ones kept
only some portions of the word are used, not all of it

parts.note: letters one, three and five of the word
mud is soil soaked with water

explanation.surface: A garden after rain: someone covered in muddy blotches from the wettest patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' reads as strange in the surface, but it means the odd-numbered letters. 'wet earth' is a plain description, not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a blurred dirty mark, so something smudgy is marked with such smears and stains.

clue.text: Killed in action leading under wild salvo in European republic

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece going under another follows it, one leading below the other
something wild is out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
KIA is the standard military abbreviation for killed in action

explanation.surface: A war report: a soldier killed in action under a wild artillery salvo somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the abbreviation for killed in action goes under the rearranged volley, finishing the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovakia is an independent state in central Europe, a republic since splitting from Czechoslovakia in 1993.

clue.text: In Paris, one French female who's outspoken and explicit

parts.note: the French word for one, in its feminine form
still in Paris: the French word for who
a vocal person speaks out freely

explanation.surface: A frank Parisienne who speaks her mind and leaves nothing unsaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' tells you to translate into French, and 'female' picks UNE rather than UN; the same French setting turns 'who' into QUI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unequivocal leaves no doubt or ambiguity, just as an explicit statement is stated clearly and openly.

clue.text: Eat snacks during the day, mostly in Austrian city

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to graze is to nibble small amounts throughout the day rather than eat proper meals

explanation.surface: A tourist snacking all day while visiting an Austrian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb for constant snacking loses its last letter to leave the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Graz is the second-largest city in Austria and the capital of the province of Styria.

clue.text: Dull bank payment system backed cover

indicators.note: going back means running from the end to the start, so the whole string runs right to left

parts.note: drab means dull and colourless
BACS is the UK system banks use for direct debits and automated transfers

explanation.surface: A complaint that a bank's payments setup is tedious and was backed by some insurance cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are written down together and the whole lot is turned round. BACS (Bankers' Automated Clearing Services) runs UK direct debits and salary payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath that encloses and protects the blade of a sword.

clue.text: Happy laughs from Charles in the States with comedian Dawson

parts.note: Chuck is the usual American nickname for Charles
Les Dawson was a British TV comedian famous for deadpan mother-in-law jokes

explanation.surface: An American called Charles shares a joke with Les Dawson and they laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Dawson, a British comedian of the 1970s and 80s, supplies his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuckles are quiet, contented laughs, the sound a pleased person makes under their breath.

clue.text: Buttoned up about one inept slob

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or moved round, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a lazy, incompetent slob who refused to say anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inept' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the material; 'about' does that job, working on the numeral plus both words.
explanation.definitionFit: To button up is to keep quiet, and biting one's lip means stopping oneself from saying something.

clue.text: Member in bar, musing

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning the gap

parts.note: the end of the first word joins the start of the second

explanation.surface: A club member sitting thoughtfully in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club member at the bar, but it means a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is a limb of the body in an old or formal sense, and an arm is one such limb.

clue.text: Democrat, hopeful, hugging wife, nodding

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap arms around, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: rosy prospects are hopeful ones
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An optimistic Democrat politician embracing his wife and nodding along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nodding' reads as agreement in the surface, but it is the head dropping as sleep comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nodding off is falling asleep, so a nodding person is sleepy and heavy-eyed.

clue.text: Series of six having ten in front

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as something is placed in a box

parts.note: the head of a queue or procession is its front
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A sequence of six items with a ten placed at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten in front' looks like an instruction to put ten first, but 'in' asks for the numeral inside a word for front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexad is a group or set of six, from the Greek root for six, as in hexagon.

clue.text: Greatly impress from end to end of Scottish loch

parts.note: all over a place means throughout it, from one end to the other
Loch Awe is a long freshwater loch in Argyll, Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone stunned by the view along the full length of a Highland loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Awe in the western Highlands is one of Scotland's longest lochs, so the surface view really is impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe someone is to subdue or overwhelm them with a strong sense of wonder or respect.

clue.text: Muppet dancing round, fast

indicators.note: dancers move about, so these letters swap places freely

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A Muppet puppet doing a quick spin on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The round letter joins the puppet before the shuffle; 'round' looks like part of the dance but is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-tempo describes music played at a quick, lively pace, so it means fast in a musical sense.

clue.text: Pale blue sign. Not half

indicators.note: without half of it, so the back half of the letters goes

parts.note: Aquarius, the water carrier, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A note about a pale blue sign, with a jokey British 'not half!' meaning 'absolutely!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it literally removes half of an eight-letter star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is a light greenish-blue colour, named from the Latin for water.

clue.text: Pilates exercises causing accidents with the rig

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Pilates move in which the body folds up and down like a pocket knife
second meaning: an articulated lorry folds in on itself in a crash

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a noun plural, the second a verb, and the one spelling serves both; 'rig' is an articulated lorry or truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding pocket knife gives its name both to a body-folding fitness move and to a lorry cab folding against its trailer.

clue.text: French fifth son comes in, say, visiting often

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for French

indicators.note: to come in is to enter, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which is what 'say' means here
Quentin comes from the Latin for fifth and was traditionally given to a fifth child

explanation.surface: A French family's fifth son keeps dropping in for frequent visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French fifth son' looks like one phrase, but French gives only its abbreviation; the name meaning fifth then goes inside the abbreviation for 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to go there habitually, so frequenting is regularly calling at it.

clue.text: Almost in fun, get nine reconditioned turbo-props

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as an object goes in a box
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a jest is a joke, something said in fun

indicators.note: something reconditioned is rebuilt, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A light-hearted plan to obtain nine overhauled propeller engines.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke word loses its last letter and the rearranged pair of words goes inside it. A turbo-prop is a jet turbine driving a propeller, so it counts as a jet engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbo-props are gas-turbine engines turning propellers, a type of jet engine used on many smaller aircraft.

clue.text: Seeing that is part of the landscape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: considering or given that, as a phrase introducing a reason
second meaning: visible within the scene before you

explanation.surface: Pointing out that something forms a feature of the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing that' reads as a conjunction, 'because', which matches the phrase 'in view of'; the second sense is literal sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both considering a fact and being visible within the scene someone can see.

clue.text: Pop singer's genealogical tree about me as subject getting justice

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: the Tree of Jesse depicts Christ's ancestry descending from Jesse, father of King David
I is the subject form of me
J is the abbreviation for Justice, as in a judge's title

explanation.surface: A pop star's family tree, written about herself, finally getting fair treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tree of Jesse is a church art motif showing Jesus's lineage; 'me as subject' asks for the grammatical subject form of 'me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessie J is an English singer-songwriter known for chart hits such as Price Tag and Bang Bang.

clue.text: Coming soon — about 10.10 — small talk finishes

indicators.note: about can mean moved around, so the letters change order

parts.note: ten written once as a word and once as the Roman numeral X
wee is Scottish and informal British for small

indicators.note: a finish is an ending, so only the closing letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A schedule announcing something coming up at about ten past ten, when the chit-chat is over.
explanation.walkthrough: '10.10' looks like a clock time, but it is two tens to be written different ways. 'small talk' looks like one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening next week is due within days, which is a fair sense of coming before long.

clue.text: Part of speech roughly suggests cost of the meal

indicators.note: spoken out loud it is only approximately like the word, so sound is the guide

parts.note: a prefix is a part added to the front of a word

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which a part of speech hints at the bill for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' wants to be a noun or verb, but the part needed is a word-beginning; 'roughly' admits the French pronunciation is only close.
explanation.definitionFit: A prix fixe is a set menu at a fixed price, French for 'fixed price', so it names what the meal costs.

clue.text: Planned school by eastern sea

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
E is the abbreviation for eastern
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A purpose-built school sited beside an eastern sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planned school' reads as a planned building; in fact 'Planned' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To scheme is to devise a plan, often a crafty one, so schemed means plotted or planned.

clue.text: A drop of the hard stuff for the lolly-eater, reportedly

definitions.text: A drop of the hard stuff

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the sound matters

parts.note: someone eating an ice lolly licks it

explanation.surface: Offering a nip of spirits to someone sucking an ice lolly.
explanation.walkthrough: A lolly is an ice lolly, a frozen treat on a stick (a popsicle in the US), which is licked.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard stuff is strong alcohol, and liquor is distilled spirits such as whisky or gin.

clue.text: Intellectual's hearty laugh at home

parts.note: a boff is a loud belly laugh, especially in theatre slang
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: A clever person laughing heartily in their own house.
explanation.walkthrough: BOFFIN is British slang for a scientist or brainy expert; 'boff' for a big laugh is mainly American showbiz slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is an informal British term for a scientist or highly knowledgeable person, a brainy type.

clue.text: Single within the boundaries of Headingley, dearie

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece goes into the other
boundaries are the edges, so only the outermost letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
single means one

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator noting a single run scored near the boundary at Headingley, the Leeds Test ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is one run and the boundary is the field's edge, so the surface is all cricket; here 'boundaries' just means first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey and dearie are both affectionate terms of address used for a loved one.

clue.text: Duty on money owed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something one is bound to do
second meaning: a debt, a bond or financial commitment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty on' looks like a tax charged on something, but 'on' just joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a moral or legal requirement and a financial liability such as a bond or debt.

clue.text: Form of chalcedony — some chalcedony unknown

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the opening run of letters is dropped and the rest kept

parts.note: the last three letters of the word, the first seven being discarded
X is the classic unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A geology note about a mineral variety and an unidentified sample.
explanation.walkthrough: The same mineral name appears twice, once as the definition and once as the source of letters, which is unusually cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a fine-grained quartz mineral used for cameos and carvings.

clue.text: Instrument from borders of Zaire — twice

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outermost letters are used
the selected letters are written down two times in a row

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A musical instrument brought from the frontiers of Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of edge letters is repeated to make four. Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: The zeze is a stringed instrument of East and Central Africa, a fiddle or stick zither.

clue.text: Blaze on headland with no main road to Italians' city

parts.note: a blaze is a fire

indicators.note: without something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: a naze is a headland or promontory, as in the Naze in Essex
an A road is a main road in Britain

explanation.surface: A fire on a clifftop with no main road leading to an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (main) and B (minor), so a main road is A. The answer is the Italian name for Florence, hence 'Italians''.
explanation.definitionFit: Firenze is what Italians call Florence, the Tuscan capital, so it is their name for the city.

clue.text: Trumpeter's drink

indicators.note: the possessive says the thing belongs to, and so is held within, the word before it

parts.note: letters two to four of the word

explanation.surface: A brass player's tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive does the work: the drink is literally the trumpeter's because it lies inside the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane or molasses, a common alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Retired professors backing the engineers, at heart British

indicators.note: going backwards means reading from right to left

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the middle letters are taken

parts.note: the three central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Old academics who now support Britain's engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like supporting in the surface, but it turns the army engineers' abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti is the Latin plural of emeritus, the title kept by professors after retirement.

clue.text: Poor Sam A. Keen and his double?

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the full stop

explanation.surface: Pity for a hard-up man named Sam A. Keen and his lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'double' is loose: someone sharing your name is a double only in name.
explanation.definitionFit: A namesake shares a person's name, a kind of double in naming rather than looks.

clue.text: Struggle eating poultry produce? I would

definitions.text: Struggle eating poultry produce? I would

indicators.note: to eat is to take something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
hens lay eggs

explanation.surface: Someone debating whether to eat eggs, and deciding they would.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: a vegetarian, unlike a vegan, will happily eat eggs, so this person says 'I would'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie is an informal British term for a vegetarian, who avoids meat but typically still eats eggs.
